successCriteria.description: An `AuthSession` type exists in the auth module with the exact canonical shape `{ token: string; profile: EmployeeProfile; status: AuthSessionStatus }`, importing `EmployeeProfile` and `AuthSessionStatus` from `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` rather than re-declaring them.

`AuthService.login(email, password)` calls `apiClient.login`, persists the returned token via `tokenStorage.setToken`, and resolves an `AuthSession` whose `status` is `AuthSessionStatus.AUTHENTICATED` and whose `token`/`profile` come from the API response.

On login failure, `AuthService.login` surfaces the server's error message verbatim (the `ApiError.message`) and adds no email-existence hint — no distinction between wrong-email and wrong-password is introduced anywhere in the module.
`AuthService.logout()` clears the token via `tokenStorage.clear()` and returns the session to an anonymous state (no authenticated token/profile remains).

`AuthProvider`/`useAuth()` hold the current `AuthSession` in React state (no state-management library), expose `login`, `logout`, and the current session, and on mount initialize an authenticated session when a token already exists in storage (re-fetching the profile via `getMe`).

Vitest unit tests cover `AuthService.login` success (token stored + authenticated session returned), login failure (server message surfaced with no email-existence hint), and `logout` (token cleared).

constraints: The auth module must import `EmployeeProfile`, `AuthSessionStatus`, and `LoginResponse` from `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` and `IApiClient`/`ITokenStorage` from `web/src/infrastructure/api/index.ts` — never re-declare these types or import from module internals.

`AuthService` must depend only on the injected `IApiClient` and `ITokenStorage`; it must not import `sessionStorage`, `fetch`, or any pool/client directly, and must not decode the JWT or inspect token expiry client-side.
Login failure must not reveal whether the email exists: surface `ApiError.message` as-is and add no email-existence hint, no wrong-email vs wrong-password branching, and no extra error text.

A failed login must not assume the stored token was cleared — the login path is unauthenticated, so the API client does not auto-clear storage on a 401 from login; the service must not clear the token on login failure.
The auth context must hold session state in React state only — no state-management library, no UI component library.
Tests must use Vitest with jsdom, globals enabled, and the existing `setupFiles`/`setupTests.ts`; imports come from `vitest`.
outOfScope: No presentation layer, routing, route guards, or pages are built in this phase — the auth context is consumed by Phase 5, not wired to any UI here.
No employee/leave/balance service modules (Phase 4) and no proactive JWT-expiry detection — the frontend relies solely on the server's 401, which is handled by the API client, not the auth module.
No backend changes: nothing under `src/` is modified, and no new SQL schema, tables, or repositories are introduced.

ambiguities.description: The concrete representation of the logged-out state is unresolved: after `logout()` (and before any login), should the context expose `null` (no `AuthSession` object) or a non-null `AuthSession` whose `status` is `AuthSessionStatus.ANONYMOUS`? This is a representation choice, distinct from the already-settled decision that `AuthSessionStatus` (including `ANONYMOUS`) is the enum to use.
options: null session (no AuthSession object when not authenticated)
AuthSession with status: AuthSessionStatus.ANONYMOUS and empty token/profile

entityInvariants.invariant: An `AuthSession` is always exactly `{ token: string; profile: EmployeeProfile; status: AuthSessionStatus }`; `status` is `AUTHENTICATED` when a valid token+profile are held, and the session is cleared (no token/profile) when the user is logged out. `profile` never carries `passwordHash` or `terminationDate`.

The anonymous/not-authenticated state is represented consistently across the service and the context provider — a single representation (either a `null` session or a session with `status: AuthSessionStatus.ANONYMOUS`) is used everywhere, never mixed.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On failure, propagate the server's error message verbatim (ApiError.message) with no email-existence hint; do not clear the stored token on failure.
Clears the token and returns to the anonymous state; must not throw and must be safe to call when already logged out.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: `AuthSession` must reuse `EmployeeProfile` and `AuthSessionStatus` exactly as declared (field-for-field, no additions/omissions/renames) rather than re-declaring them.
`AuthService` must consume `IApiClient.login`/`IApiClient.getMe` and `ITokenStorage.setToken`/`clear` exactly as declared, and treat `ApiError` as the only error type thrown by API calls.
The token persistence key and semantics must match the existing `TokenStorage` (sessionStorage under `trackeros.token`); the auth module must not introduce a second storage mechanism.

integrationPoints.why: AuthService delegates login/getMe to the API client and token persistence to token storage; the API client is the single source of the bearer header and 401-clearing behaviour.
AuthSession and the login return value are assembled from these canonical shared types.
The auth context's `login`/`logout`/session are the single source the presentation layer will consume for guards and the login/logout flow.
